title: Estonia Digital Nomad Visa: How to Apply and Requirements | Grey
summary: Estonia was the first country to launch a digital nomad visa. Income requirements, costs, documents and the full application process explained. Apply now.
body_markdown:
While under the radar, Estonia is gradually becoming the world’s most advanced digital society. From e-governance to robust support for start-ups like Skype, Wise, and Bolt, Estonia now consistently ranks among the top digital nomad destinations in Europe. Once a country has good infrastructure and tech companies, all that is left for a digital nomad is low living costs and a city to explore.


Estonia launched the world's first digital nomad visa in August 2020, allowing remote workers to live in the country for up to one year. Applicants must earn at least €4,500 per month and work for an employer or clients outside Estonia. The visa gives access to the Schengen Area for the duration of the stay.


This article explores Estonia’s digital nomad visa, the cost, requirements, application process and everything else you need as a digital nomad visiting Estonia.


## What is the Estonian digital nomad visa?


Estonia was the first country in the world to introduce a formal digital nomad visa in August 2020. The visa allows non-EU and non-EEA nationals to live and work remotely in Estonia for up to one year, provided their income comes from an employer or clients based outside Estonia.


During the stay, digital nomad visa holders also have access to the broader Schengen Area. So, they can travel freely within the 27 Schengen member states for up to 90 days.


It is important to clarify that the Estonian digital nomad visa is entirely different from Estonia's e-Residency programme. E-Residency is a digital identity programme that allows non-Estonians to register and manage an EU-based company online. It does not grant the right to live in Estonia, travel within the EU, or obtain any form of residence. Many readers searching for the digital nomad visa encounter e-Residency and conflate the two. They serve different purposes and require separate applications.


The digital nomad visa is for physical residence in Estonia. E-Residency is for digital business registration. You can hold one, the other, both, or neither.

## Estonia digital nomad visa requirements


Here are the requirements to qualify for an Estonian digital nomad visa. These requirements might vary by jurisdiction and specific scenarios. Review the requirements with the[consulate in your jurisdiction](https://www.politsei.ee/en) to understand.


- **Nationality:** Non-EU and non-EEA citizens. EU and EEA nationals do not require a visa to live and work in Estonia.
- **Income threshold:** A[minimum gross monthly income of €4,500](https://www.e-resident.gov.ee/blog/posts/faqs-about-estonias-digital-nomad-visa/) (approximately $5,150 or £3,900 as at June 2026). Income must be location-independent and earned from an employer or clients based outside Estonia.
- **Remote work arrangement:** The applicant must demonstrate that their work can be performed from any location, either as a remote employee of a foreign company or as a self-employed professional with clients outside Estonia.
- **Health insurance:** Valid comprehensive health insurance covering the Schengen Area for the full duration of the intended stay.
- **Clean criminal record:** A criminal background check from the applicant's country of residence and any other country where they have lived for more than 12 months in the past five years.
- **Financial self-sufficiency:** Proof that the applicant can support themselves without seeking local Estonian employment or accessing Estonian social benefits.


## Required documents


Prepare the following before contacting the Estonian embassy or consulate. Incomplete applications cause delays and may be returned without processing.


- Valid passport with at least six months of validity beyond the intended end of the stay, and sufficient blank pages for stamps
- Completed visa application form, available from the Estonian embassy or consulate website
- Two recent passport-sized photographs meeting the embassy's specifications
- Proof of income: three to six months of payslips, bank statements demonstrating consistent income above the threshold, or client contracts with payment terms and invoices supporting the stated income level
- Employer letter or client contracts confirming the remote nature of the work arrangement and that the employer or clients are based outside Estonia
- Health insurance certificate covering the Schengen Area for the full duration of the intended stay, with a coverage minimum meeting the Schengen standard (currently €30,000)
- Criminal background check from the relevant authorities in the applicant's country of residence
- Proof of accommodation in Estonia, such as a signed lease, confirmed rental, or letter of invitation from a host
- Application fee payment


Self-employed applicants should also include business registration documents, evidence of client relationships, and at least six months of income history demonstrating consistent earnings above the threshold.

## How to apply: step by step


1. **Confirm eligibility:** Check that your income meets the current threshold, your work qualifies as location-independent, and your nationality requires a visa to reside in Estonia. If you are an EU or EEA citizen, you do not need to apply.
2. **Gather all documents:** Use the list above as your checklist. Every document should be accurate, complete, and consistent with the others. Income figures on bank statements should match those referenced in employment letters or client contracts.
3. **Contact the Estonian embassy or consulate in your home country:** Applications are submitted in person at the Estonian embassy or consulate in the country where you are a citizen or legal resident. Some countries may offer an online pre-application step. Verify from the specific embassy website whether this applies to your location, as the process varies by country.
4. **Submit your application:** Attend your appointment, submit all original documents along with copies, and pay the visa fee. The officer may ask questions about your work, client relationships, and plans in Estonia.
5. **Wait for the decision:** Processing typically takes 15 to 30 days from the date of submission, though it can be longer during peak periods or if the consulate requests additional documentation. Do not book non-refundable travel until the visa is confirmed.
6. **Travel to Estonia:** Upon approval, the entry visa is issued. Once in Estonia, register your address at the local government office. If you intend to stay beyond the initial visa period, you must apply for a temporary residence permit, which carries its own requirements.

## Costs, duration and what to know about tax


- **Application fee:** Approximately €80 to €100, depending on the applicant's nationality. Verify the current fee from your specific embassy before applying, as fees differ by country of origin and may change. The fee is non-refundable if the application is unsuccessful.
- **Duration:** The digital nomad visa is issued for up to one year. It is not renewable within Estonia. To return to the same programme, the applicant must leave the Schengen Area and submit a new application from their home country.
- **Schengen travel:** During the visa period, holders can travel freely within the Schengen Area. The standard 90-day rule that applies to most non-EU tourists does not apply to digital nomad visa holders during their permitted stay, as the visa grants a right of residence in Estonia.
- **Tax position:** Staying in Estonia for more than 183 days in a calendar year may trigger[Estonian tax residency](https://grey.co/blog/digital-nomad-tax) under domestic rules, making worldwide income taxable in Estonia. Many digital nomad visa holders plan their stay to remain below that threshold. However, tax residency rules interact with your home country's tax obligations and any applicable tax treaty between Estonia and your home country. This is not legal tax advice. Verify your individual position with a qualified tax adviser familiar with Estonian and international tax rules before committing to a long-term stay.

## Frequently asked questions


### **Is Estonia e-Residency the same as the digital nomad visa?**


No. They are completely separate programmes. E-Residency is a digital identity programme that allows non-Estonians to register and manage an Estonian company online. It does not provide the right to live in Estonia, travel in the Schengen Area, or hold any form of residence status. The digital nomad visa is a physical residence authorisation that allows you to live in Estonia for up to one year. You can hold both, but they serve entirely different purposes.


### **Can I travel to other Schengen countries on the Estonia digital nomad visa?**


Yes. The visa grants access to the Schengen Area for the duration of your permitted stay. You can travel freely within Schengen member states. Estonia must remain your primary country of residence under the visa, but short stays in other Schengen countries are permitted.


### **Can I extend the Estonia digital nomad visa?**


The digital nomad visa itself is not renewable within Estonia. If you want to remain in Estonia beyond the one-year period, you would need to leave the Schengen Area and apply for a new visa from your home country, or explore other long-stay options available under Estonian immigration law. Check with the Estonian Police and Border Guard Board for any updates to this process.


### **Can I bring my family on the Estonia digital nomad visa?**


Family members cannot automatically accompany the primary visa holder under the digital nomad visa. Spouses and dependants would need to apply for their own appropriate visas to join the primary holder in Estonia. Check with the Estonian embassy in your country for the current options available for family reunification alongside a digital nomad visa.


### **Do I pay tax in Estonia on the digital nomad visa?**


Staying in Estonia for more than 183 days in a calendar year may trigger tax residency under Estonian domestic law. Estonian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income. Staying below 183 days in the calendar year reduces this risk, but tax residency depends on multiple factors, including the structure of your stay and your home country's tax rules. Consult a tax adviser with expertise in Estonian and international tax before making long-stay plans.


### **Is Estonia a good base for digital nomads?**


Estonia consistently ranks among the top digital nomad destinations in Europe. Tallinn offers high-quality internet infrastructure, a dense concentration of tech companies and startups, a compact and walkable old city, and a cost of living meaningfully lower than Western European capitals. The country's digital infrastructure is among the most advanced in the EU, and e-government services are extensive. The winters are cold and dark, which suits some nomads and deters others. Overall, it remains one of the more practical and well-supported environments for remote workers in Europe.
